branches.en: A bench turning a dispute into a rule.
branches.cn: 法官席把争执变成一条规则。

branches.en: A knot cut by a written line.
branches.cn: 一个结被一行文字剪断。

branches.en: One voice making a rule for many.
branches.cn: 一个声音为许多人定下规则。

branches.en: All four are a decision that has been made binding on others.
branches.cn: 四者都是已经对他人产生约束力的决定。

intro.en: Decree is de- plus cernere; the sifting and cutting roots build many decision words.
intro.cn: decree 由 de- 加 cernere 构成；筛与切这两个词根造出许多决定类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere means to sift and caedere means to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛，caedere 意为切。

definition_zh: 妊娠期；孕育过程；（想法、作品的）酝酿期
definition_en: the period or process of carrying young in the womb, or a period of development before something is produced
core_image: 一块记着日期的木牌挂在栏边，从配种那天到生产那天，中间是一段被等待填满的时间
scene: 在动物园的饲养记录里，管理员写下日期后说： Gestation in this species lasts about eleven months.
sceneCN: 这里 gestation 指「从受孕到生产的妊娠期长度」（第 3 个义项：妊娠持续时间）；句意是这个物种的妊娠期约为十一个月。

senses.title: The carrying of young in the womb
senses.titleCN: 在子宫内孕育幼体的过程
senses.definition: the process of carrying a developing young inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 在体内携带发育中幼体的过程
senses.example: Gestation begins with implantation and ends with birth.
senses.exampleCN: 妊娠从着床开始，到出生结束。
senses.why: Gestare means to carry, so gestation is literally the carrying of young, the process rather than the count of days.
senses.whyCN: gestare 意为「携带」，因此 gestation 字面就是携带幼体，指过程而非天数。

senses.title: Pregnancy as a state
senses.definition: the state of being pregnant
senses.definitionCN: 怀孕的状态
senses.example: Nutrition during gestation affects the young's later health.
senses.exampleCN: 妊娠期间的营养影响幼体日后的健康。
senses.why: The process can also be viewed as a condition a body is in, so the noun names the state as well.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程也可视为身体所处的一种状态，因此这个名词也指状态。

senses.title: The length of pregnancy
senses.definition: the period from conception to birth, measured in days or weeks
senses.definitionCN: 从受孕到出生的时间，以日或周计
senses.example: Gestation in this species lasts about eleven months.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的妊娠期约为十一个月。
senses.why: Once measured, the carrying process becomes a duration, and the noun names the number of days.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被测量，孕育过程就变成一个时长，这个名词便指天数。

senses.title: Animal gestation
senses.definition: the carrying period of a non-human animal
senses.definitionCN: 非人类动物的孕育期
senses.example: Elephant gestation is among the longest of any land mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 大象的妊娠期是陆生哺乳动物中最长的之一。
senses.why: The same biological process receives the same noun across mammals, with the length varying by species.
senses.whyCN: 同一生物过程在不同哺乳动物中用同一名词，长度随物种而变。

senses.title: The incubation of an idea
senses.definition: the period during which an idea or plan develops before it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 想法或计划在呈现之前的发展时期
senses.example: The proposal had a long gestation before it reached the board.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案在送到董事会之前经历了漫长的酝酿。
senses.why: An idea is pictured as being carried unseen, exactly as a body carries young, until it is ready to be born.
senses.whyCN: 想法被想象为被看不见地携带，正像身体携带幼体，直到可以出生。

senses.title: Internal development in viviparous animals
senses.definition: development inside the mother's body rather than in an egg
senses.definitionCN: 在母体内而非卵内的发育
senses.example: Viviparity extends gestation beyond the egg stage.
senses.exampleCN: 胎生使孕育延伸到卵阶段之后。
senses.why: Zoology uses the noun to mark the internal route of development, contrasted with laying eggs.
senses.whyCN: 动物学用这个名词标记体内发育路径，与产卵相对。

senses.title: Gestational age in obstetrics
senses.definition: the age of a pregnancy measured from the last menstrual period
senses.definitionCN: 从末次月经起算的妊娠时长
senses.example: Gestation is counted from the last menstrual period, not from conception.
senses.exampleCN: 孕龄从末次月经起算，而非从受孕起算。
senses.why: Clinical practice needs a fixed starting point, so the noun becomes a measurement convention.
senses.whyCN: 临床实践需要固定起点，这个名词于是成为一种测量约定。

senses.title: The incubation of a work of art
senses.definition: the period in which a work or project is formed before it appears
senses.definitionCN: 作品或项目在问世之前形成的时期
senses.example: The novel's gestation took a decade of notes and revisions.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的酝酿花了十年笔记与修改。
senses.why: Creative work also ripens unseen, and the biological metaphor gives that invisible period a name.
senses.whyCN: 创作也在看不见处成熟，生物比喻给这段不可见时期一个名称。

intro.en: Gestation comes from Latin gestatio, a carrying, from gestare to carry, a frequentative of gerere to carry or bear; the deeper origin of gerere is uncertain.
intro.cn: gestation 来自拉丁 gestatio「携带」，出自 gestare「携带」，后者是 gerere「携带、承担」的反复动词；gerere 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Gerere meant to carry, bear or manage; its deeper origin is not established, and the many senses of the English descendants reflect that breadth.
items.cn: gerere 意为携带、承担、管理；其更深来源未得到证明，英语后裔的多种词义正反映这种宽度。

items.en: Gestare was a frequentative of gerere, meaning to carry about or keep carrying, which suits the long carrying of young.
items.cn: gestare 是 gerere 的反复动词，意为「反复携带、带在身上」，正合长期孕育幼体。

items.en: Gestatio named a carrying or being carried, and in medical Latin the carrying of young in the womb.
items.cn: gestatio 指携带或被携带，在医学拉丁语中指在子宫内孕育幼体。

items.en: English gestation appeared in the early seventeenth century, first for the carrying of young and soon after for the period itself.
items.cn: 英语 gestation 在 17 世纪初出现，先指孕育幼体，随后很快指这一时期本身。

items.en: Later writers applied the word to the slow formation of ideas, books and projects.
items.cn: 后来的作者把这个词用于想法、书籍与项目的缓慢形成。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of Latin gerere is unresolved, so any Indo-European base offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（gerere 词根存疑、年代为约数）：拉丁 gerere 的更深来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语基均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the Latin carrying root that are easily confused; group two holds terms for pregnancy and for slow formation.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「携带」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是妊娠与缓慢形成的近义术语。

entries.definition: To carry young or develop an idea; the verb is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 孕育幼体或酝酿想法；动词是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: Relating to gestation, especially to age or diabetes in pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 与妊娠有关的，尤指孕龄或妊娠期糖尿病。

entries.definition: From gestus, a bearing or movement of the body, also from gerere; it shares the root but means a movement, not a carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 gestus「身体的姿态或动作」，同样出自 gerere；共享词根，但指动作而非携带。

entries.definition: From digerere, to carry apart or dissolve, built on the same gerere; it distributes rather than carries young.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 digerere「分开运送、消解」，同出 gerere；它是分解分配，而非孕育。

entries.definition: The condition of carrying young; it names the state more plainly than gestation, which often names the period.
entries.definitionCN: 携带幼体的状态；比 gestation 更直白地指状态，而 gestation 常指时期。

entries.definition: Sitting on eggs or, figuratively, letting something develop; it is the closest word for the idea sense.
entries.definitionCN: 孵卵，或比喻让某物发展；是「想法」义最接近的词。

entries.definition: The medical state of being pregnant, from Latin gravis heavy; it is a clinical synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 怀孕的医学状态，来自拉丁 gravis「重」；是临床近义词。

entries.definition: The length of a pregnancy, as in full term; it names the measured span that gestation can also denote.
entries.definitionCN: 妊娠的长度，如足月；它指 gestation 也可表示的测量时长。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Gestare to carry plus -tion: the carrying of young.
normal.cn: gestare「携带」加 -tion：携带幼体。

normal.en: The family runs gestate, gestation, gestational, gestationally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gestate、gestation、gestational、gestationally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: gestation period, length of gestation, during gestation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：妊娠期、妊娠时长、妊娠期间。

normal.en: The verb gestate also covers ideas and books.
normal.cn: 动词 gestate 也涵盖想法与书。

normal.en: Same root, different branches: gesture and digestion.
normal.cn: 同根不同枝：gesture 与 digestion。

abstract.en: Picture a dated board by a pen, counting days from mating to birth.
abstract.cn: 想象栏边一块记日期的牌子，从配种数到生产。

abstract.en: Picture a manuscript carried unseen for ten years before it opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手稿被看不见地携带十年才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a pot on a low flame that must not be hurried.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小火上的锅，急不得。

examples.en: Elephant gestation lasts nearly two years.
examples.cn: 大象的妊娠期接近两年。

examples.en: The policy had a long gestation and many drafts.
examples.cn: 这项政策经历了漫长的酝酿与许多草案。

examples.en: Gestational diabetes is usually tested for late in the second trimester.
examples.cn: 妊娠期糖尿病通常在第二孕期后期筛查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gest 携带 + ation 过程」——把幼体带在身上的一段时间 → 妊娠期、酝酿期

root: 拉丁 gestatio「携带」← gestare「携带」（gerere「携带、承担」的反复动词）；gerere 更深来源不确定，英语首见年代约 17 世纪初。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one carrying: the process, the state, the measured length, the animal case, the incubation of an idea, internal development, clinical dating and the ripening of a work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「携带」展开：过程、状态、测得的时长、动物情形、想法酝酿、体内发育、临床计时与作品成熟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dated board counting the days between mating and birth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块记日期的牌子，数着配种到生产的每一天。

branches.en: PREGNANCY STATE: carrying young is also a condition one is in.
branches.cn: 妊娠状态：孕育幼体也是一种持续所处的状态。

branches.en: MEASURED TIME: days, species differences and clinical starting points turn carrying into a number.
branches.cn: 被测量的时间：天数、物种差异与临床起点把孕育变成数字。

branches.en: IDEA INCUBATION: a plan is carried unseen until it is ready.
branches.cn: 想法的酝酿：计划在被看见之前一直默默孕育。

branches.en: INTERNAL ROUTE: gestation marks development inside the body rather than in an egg.
branches.cn: 体内路径：gestation 标记体内发育而非卵内发育。

branches.en: HELD INSIDE: from a child to a work, something is carried before it appears.
branches.cn: 内含之孕：从胎儿到作品，都是先被孕育再被呈现。

intro.en: Gestation is a Latin frequentative verb turned into a noun, and the same carrying root builds several words with very different meanings.
intro.cn: gestation 是一个拉丁反复动词变来的名词，同一个「携带」词根构成若干意义很不同的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere gives gestare, gestation, gesture and digestion; the frequentative gestare adds the sense of repeated or sustained carrying.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gerere 衍生 gestare、gestation、gesture 与 digestion；反复动词 gestare 增添「反复或持续携带」之义。

items.example: The verb is the base of a wide family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是一个大词族的基础。

items.example: Gestare supplied the idea of sustained carrying.
items.exampleCN: gestare 提供持续携带的观念。

items.example: Gestatio entered medical Latin for pregnancy.
items.exampleCN: gestatio 以妊娠义进入医学拉丁语。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。
这里的妊娠期持续十一个月。

items.example: A gesture can carry meaning without words.
items.exampleCN: 手势可以不靠言语携带意义。

definition_zh: 温盐的；由温度与盐度共同决定的
definition_en: relating to the combined effect of temperature and salinity, especially on the density of seawater
core_image: 两支探头伸进同一桶海水：一支量冷热，一支量咸淡，两个读数合起来决定这水有多重
scene: 海洋学讲座上，讲者把探头放进桶里刚打上来的水样说， The thermohaline contrast between the two layers keeps them apart.
sceneCN: 这里 thermohaline 指「温度与盐度合在一起造成的（差异）」（第 1 个义项：温盐的）；句意为：两层水之间的温盐差异使它们保持分离。

pos.zh: 温盐的；由温度与盐度共同决定的
用于复合术语，如温盐环流、温盐层化

forms.label: 比较级（关系形容词，罕用）
最高级（关系形容词，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 温盐环流（由本词构成的固定术语）
盐的；含盐的（与表示「盐」的希腊成分同源的独立形容词）
温跃层（共享「热」这一成分的同族术语）
盐跃层（共享「盐」这一成分的同族术语）

senses.title: Of heat and salt together
senses.definition: relating to temperature and salinity considered together as a pair of properties
senses.definitionCN: 把温度与盐度作为成对属性一并考虑的
senses.example: Every water sample has a thermohaline signature.
senses.exampleCN: 每个水样都带有温盐特征。
senses.why: Greek thermē 'heat' supplies the first half and halinos 'of salt' the second, with -ine joining them: the word names a pair, not a single quantity.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 thermē「热」提供前半，halinos「盐的」提供后半，再由 -ine 连接：这个词命名的是一对属性，而不是单一量值。

senses.title: Controlling density
senses.definition: describing the pair of properties that together fix the density of seawater
senses.definitionCN: 描述共同决定海水密度的两项属性
senses.example: Density is a thermohaline property of sea water.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是海水的一项温盐属性。
senses.why: cold water and salty water are both heavier, so heat and salt pull on the same lever; calling density thermohaline says which two dials control it.
senses.whyCN: 冷水和咸水都更重，热与盐拉的是同一根杠杆；把密度称为 thermohaline，就是说明哪两个旋钮在控制它。

senses.title: Driving the deep overturning
senses.definition: describing the temperature and salt differences that set the deep ocean circulation in motion
senses.definitionCN: 描述推动深层海洋环流运转的温度与盐度差异
senses.example: The deep flow is thermohaline in origin, not wind-driven.
senses.exampleCN: 这股深层流源于温盐作用，而不是风。
senses.why: wind moves the top of the sea, but sinking needs weight; only heat and salt can make water heavy enough to go down.
senses.whyCN: 风只动海面，下沉却需要重量；只有热与盐能让水重到可以往下走。

senses.title: Layering the water column
senses.definition: describing the layering of the water column that results from combined temperature and salinity differences
senses.definitionCN: 描述由温度与盐度差异共同造成的水柱分层
senses.example: A thermohaline boundary separates the two water masses.
senses.exampleCN: 一道温盐界面把两个水团分开。
senses.why: different heat and salt make water of different weight, and weight settles into layers instead of mixing away.
senses.whyCN: 不同的热与盐造出不同重量的水，而重量会沉淀成层，而不是混掉。

senses.title: Marking a water mass
senses.definition: describing the temperature and salinity values used to identify a particular body of water
senses.definitionCN: 描述用来辨认某一特定水体的温度与盐度数值
senses.example: Charting thermohaline properties lets a ship trace where a parcel came from.
senses.exampleCN: 测绘温盐性质能让船只追溯一块水来自何处。
senses.why: a water mass keeps the heat and salt it acquired at the surface, so the pair works as a label that travels with it.
senses.whyCN: 一个水团保留着它在表层获得的热与盐，因此这对数值成了随它旅行的标签。

senses.title: Forcing in a climate model
senses.titleCN: 气候模式中的温盐强迫
senses.definition: describing the surface fluxes of heat and fresh water that a climate model applies as thermohaline forcing
senses.definitionCN: 描述气候模式作为温盐强迫施加的热量与淡水通量
senses.example: The model applies thermohaline forcing at the high latitudes.
senses.exampleCN: 该模式在高纬地区施加温盐强迫。
senses.why: a model cannot move the ocean itself, so it must be given the heat and salt exchanges that will make water move.
senses.whyCN: 模式本身搬不动整个海洋，因此必须交给它那些会让水动起来的热量与盐分交换。

senses.title: The conveyor image
senses.definition: describing the slow global loop imagined as a conveyor belt driven by heat and salt
senses.definitionCN: 描述被想象成由热与盐驱动的全球缓慢环路
senses.example: The thermohaline conveyor is a shorthand for a loop no ship can follow in one lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐传送带是对一个没有船能在一生中走完的环路的简称。
senses.why: the loop is too slow and too large to see, so it is pictured as a belt: a mechanism, not a place.
senses.whyCN: 这个环路太慢太大，看不见，于是被画成一条传送带：一个机制，而不是一个地点。

senses.title: On a millennial clock
senses.definition: describing processes whose timescale runs to centuries or millennia rather than to seasons
senses.definitionCN: 描述时间尺度以百年或千年计而非以季节计的过程
senses.example: Thermohaline change is measured on a millennial clock.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐变化以千年的尺度来衡量。
senses.why: water that sinks must cross the whole basin before it rises, and that journey outlasts any human career.
senses.whyCN: 下沉的水要走完整个海盆才能重新上升，这段旅程比任何人的职业生涯都长。

senses.title: A signal in the sediment
senses.definition: describing ancient temperature and salinity conditions reconstructed from sediment or ice records
senses.definitionCN: 描述从沉积物或冰芯记录中重建的古代温度与盐度状况
senses.example: A thermohaline shift in the core matches the end of the cold period.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的温盐突变与寒冷期的结束相对应。
senses.why: shells and salts preserve the heat and salt of the water they formed in, so the pair becomes a readable trace of a vanished sea.
senses.whyCN: 贝壳与盐类保留着它们形成时水中的热与盐，于是这对数值成了对一片消失之海的可用痕迹。

intro.en: Thermohaline is a nineteenth-century scientific compound of two Greek stems: thermē 'heat' and hals 'salt' with its adjective halinos, joined by the English suffix -ine. It names water by the two properties that fix its density. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: thermohaline 是 19 世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊词干构成：thermē「热」与 hals「盐」（及其形容词 halinos），再用英语后缀 -ine 连接；它以决定水密度的两项属性来命名水。年代均为约数。

items.en: Thermē 'heat' comes from thermos 'hot', the stem behind thermometer and thermic; it names the state, not the fire that produces it.
items.cn: thermē「热」来自 thermos「热的」，也是 thermometer 与 thermic 的词干；它命名状态，而不是产生热的火。

items.en: Hals, halos means 'salt' and also 'sea'; the adjective halinos 'of salt' is the form English borrowed for the second half of the compound.
items.cn: hals, halos 意为「盐」，也指「海」；形容词 halinos「盐的」就是英语借来构成复合词后半的形式。

items.en: The adjective ending -ine, from Latin -inus and French -ine, was the standard way nineteenth-century science turned a noun into a property adjective.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -ine 来自拉丁 -inus 与法语 -ine，是 19 世纪科学把名词变成性质形容词的标准手段。

items.en: Physical oceanography needed a word for the pair of controls on density, and the Greek stems were joined rather than a phrase invented; the compound names what it measures.
items.cn: 物理海洋学需要一个词指控制密度的这对因素，于是把希腊词干拼接起来，而不是另造短语；这个复合词命名了它所测量的东西。

items.en: The compound became familiar through thermohaline circulation and the conveyor image, so the adjective now usually appears attached to circulation or stratification.
items.cn: 这个复合词通过温盐环流与传送带意象而为人熟知，因此如今这个形容词通常与 circulation 或 stratification 连用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner, not the roots): the exact author and year of the first use are not established, and the PIE sources of both thermos and hals are reconstructions rather than attested forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指首见年代与造词者，不涉及词根）：最早用例的作者与年份没有定论；thermos 与 hals 的印欧来源均为重构形式，而非有文献可查的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share one of the two Greek halves; group two holds words about salt, heat, density and layering that each cover only part of the idea.
note.cn: 第一组是共享两个希腊成分之一的词；第二组是关于盐、热、密度与分层的词，各自只覆盖这一概念的一部分。

entries.definition: relating to heat alone; it comes from the same Greek thermē but says nothing about salt.
entries.definitionCN: 只与热有关；同出希腊 thermē，却完全不涉及盐。

entries.definition: of or containing salt; it is the second half of thermohaline standing alone, with no heat in it.
entries.definitionCN: 盐的、含盐的；它是 thermohaline 的后半单独成词，其中没有热。

entries.definition: a layer of rapid temperature change in water; it shares therm- but names a boundary, not a pair of properties.
entries.definitionCN: 水中温度急剧变化的一层；共享 therm-，但命名的是一个界面，而不是一对属性。

entries.definition: a layer of rapid salinity change; it is the salt counterpart of the thermocline, and again a boundary rather than a property pair.
entries.definitionCN: 盐度急剧变化的一层；它是温跃层的盐度对应物，同样是一个界面而非一对属性。

entries.definition: containing salt; it measures one half of what thermohaline measures and ignores temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的；它只涉及 thermohaline 所量的一半，不涉及温度。

entries.definition: mass per unit volume; thermohaline properties are what make seawater density vary, so density is the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 单位体积的质量；温盐性质是使海水密度变化的原因，因此密度是结果。

entries.definition: the arrangement of water in layers; thermohaline differences produce it, but the word itself says nothing about heat or salt.
entries.definitionCN: 水成层排列的状态；温盐差异造成这种排列，但这个词本身不涉及热或盐。

entries.definition: the upward force a fluid exerts; thermohaline contrasts create buoyancy differences, which is how they move water.
entries.definitionCN: 流体施加的向上之力；温盐差异造成浮力差，从而推动水运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: therm- is heat: thermometer, thermal and thermocline all start here.
normal.cn: therm- 就是热：thermometer、thermal、thermocline 都从这里开始。

normal.en: hal- is salt: halite is rock salt, and haline means salty.
normal.cn: hal- 就是盐：halite 是岩盐，haline 意为含盐的。

normal.en: -ine is the adjective ending that turns a noun into a property, as in saline and marine.
normal.cn: -ine 是把名词变成性质形容词的词尾，如 saline 与 marine。

normal.en: The compound names its own cause: heat plus salt give density, and density drives the deep flow.
normal.cn: 这个复合词点明了自己的成因：热加盐给出密度，密度再驱动深层流。

normal.en: Its usual partners are fixed: thermohaline circulation, thermohaline stratification, thermohaline forcing.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭配很有限：温盐环流、温盐层化、温盐强迫。

abstract.en: Picture two dials on one bucket, one marked heat and one marked salt, both wired to the same scale.
abstract.cn: 想象桶上有两个旋钮，一个标热，一个标盐，都接到同一块刻度盘上。

abstract.en: Picture water that is too heavy to stay on top and has no choice but to sink.
abstract.cn: 想象水重得无法留在上层，除了下沉别无选择。

abstract.en: Picture a layer of water that refuses to mix with the layer beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一层水拒绝与它下面那层混合。

examples.en: Thermohaline differences make the deep water heavy enough to sink.
examples.cn: 温盐差异使深层水重到足以下沉。

examples.en: The basin's thermohaline structure changed after the ice melted.
examples.cn: 冰融化后，该海盆的温盐结构发生了改变。

examples.en: Models treat heat and fresh water as thermohaline forcing.
examples.cn: 模式把热量与淡水当作温盐强迫来处理。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词＋谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 「热么？海盐」——热与盐一起称量海水，决定它轻重 → 温盐的

root: 希腊 thermē「热」+ hals, halos「盐」的形容词 halinos「盐的」+ 英语后缀 -ine → thermohaline；19 世纪科学复合词，指温度与盐度共同作用；两个词根均属希腊语，无拉丁同族；thermē 与 hals 的更早印欧来源均为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one pair of dials: heat and salt named together, density fixed by them, sinking driven by density, layers formed, water masses labelled, model forcing supplied, the loop pictured as a belt, its slow clock, and its trace in old sediment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一对旋钮：热与盐并称、二者定下密度、密度驱动下沉、由此成层、给水团贴标签、给模式提供强迫、把环路画成传送带、它缓慢的时钟，以及它在古老沉积物中的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two gauges in the same bucket, one reading heat and one reading salt, their two numbers deciding how heavy the water is.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶水里的两支量表，一支读热，一支读盐，两个读数决定这水有多重。

branches.en: THE TWO DIALS: heat and salt are named together because together they set density.
branches.cn: 两个旋钮：热与盐并称，因为二者合力定下密度。

branches.en: WHAT MAKES WATER MOVE: the same pair drives sinking in the sea and appears as forcing in a model.
branches.cn: 让水动起来的东西：同一对因素在海里驱动下沉，在模式里则表现为强迫。

branches.en: WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND: layers in the column, and a signature that identifies a water mass.
branches.cn: 它留下的东西：水柱中的分层，以及辨认一个水团的标记。

branches.en: THE SLOW LOOP: pictured as a conveyor and measured on a millennial clock.
branches.cn: 缓慢的环路：被画成传送带，并以千年为尺度计量。

branches.en: A TRACE IN MUD: the pair survives in sediment as a record of an old sea.
branches.cn: 泥中的痕迹：这对数值在沉积物里留存，成为一片古海的记录。

intro.en: Thermohaline is a scientific compound made of two Greek roots and one English suffix; the same three pieces build the vocabulary of temperature and salt in water.
intro.cn: thermohaline 是由两个希腊词根加一个英语后缀构成的科学复合词；同样的三个构件搭建起水中温度与盐分的词汇。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative of this word: both roots are Greek, and only the suffix -ine reached English through Latin -inus and French -ine.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同族：两个词根都是希腊语，只有后缀 -ine 是经拉丁 -inus 与法语 -ine 进入英语的。

items.example: Thermē gave English the stem therm-.
items.exampleCN: thermē 给英语留下了 therm- 这个词干。

items.example: Thermos is the adjective behind thermē.
items.exampleCN: thermos 是 thermē 背后的形容词。

items.example: Hals appears in halite and in halocline.
items.exampleCN: hals 出现在 halite 与 halocline 中。

items.example: Halinos supplies the middle of the compound.
items.exampleCN: halinos 提供了这个复合词的中段。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of
items.example: Saline, marine and thermohaline share this ending.
items.exampleCN: saline、marine 与 thermohaline 共用这个词尾。

items.example: Thermohaline properties decide how dense the water is.
items.exampleCN: 温盐性质决定水有多重。

items.meaning: a layer where temperature falls sharply
items.example: The thermocline blocks mixing between two layers.
items.exampleCN: 温跃层阻隔了两层之间的混合。

items.meaning: a layer where salinity changes sharply
items.example: A halocline can keep fresh water on top of salt water.
items.exampleCN: 盐跃层能把淡水保持在咸水之上。

items.example: Haline water is denser than fresh water.
The thermometer reads the temperature of the sample.
items.exampleCN: 温度计读出样品的温度。

definition_zh: 税收收入；政府征税所得；（特定税种的）税款总额
definition_en: the total money that a government collects from taxes
core_image: 市政厅账本上最粗的一栏，由无数小格汇总成一条长条
scene: 市政厅的年度账本上，最大的一栏来自销售税与所得税。 On the city hall ledger, the largest line comes from tax revenue raised on sales and income.
sceneCN: 市政厅的年度账本上，最大的一栏来自销售税与所得税；句中的 tax revenue 指「政府通过征税取得的收入总额」（第 1 个义项：政府税收收入总额）。图中可辨识物件：账本、长条图表、税单、市政厅印章。

pos.zh: 各类税收收入；不同年度或税种的收入额

collocations.phrase: tax revenue as a share of GDP
collocations.zh: 税收收入占经济总量的比重

senses.title: The government's total tax intake
senses.definition: the whole sum of money a government receives from all forms of taxation in a period
senses.definitionCN: 政府在一段时期内从各种税种取得的全部款项
senses.example: On the city hall ledger, the largest line comes from tax revenue raised on sales and income.
senses.exampleCN: 市政厅的年度账本上，最大的一栏来自销售税与所得税。
senses.why: Tax names the charge and revenue names what comes back in, so the phrase measures money flowing toward the treasury.
senses.whyCN: tax 指课征，revenue 指回流之物，因此这个短语衡量的是流向国库的钱。

senses.title: The yield of one particular tax
senses.definition: the amount produced by a single tax, such as a fuel duty or a property levy
senses.definitionCN: 由单一税种产生的金额，如燃料税或房产税
senses.example: Fuel duty remains the steadiest source of tax revenue in the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料税仍是预算中最稳定的税收收入来源。
senses.why: A total is made of parts, so the same phrase can name the contribution of any one tax.
senses.whyCN: 总额由各部分相加而成，因此同一短语也可指任一税种的贡献。

senses.title: Revenue collected by central government
senses.titleCN: 中央或联邦政府取得的税收收入
senses.definition: tax money that goes to the national treasury rather than to local authorities
senses.definitionCN: 进入国家国库而非地方财政的税款
senses.example: Central tax revenue covers defence, while councils rely on local levies.
senses.exampleCN: 中央税收收入支撑国防，地方议会则依赖本地课征。
senses.why: Revenue follows the level of government that imposes the tax, so the phrase splits along central and local lines.
senses.whyCN: 收入跟随课征它的政府层级，因此这个短语会按中央与地方分开。

senses.title: Revenue collected by local government
senses.titleCN: 地方政府取得的税收收入
senses.definition: tax money that stays with a city, county or regional authority
senses.definitionCN: 留在市、县或地区当局的税款
senses.example: Local tax revenue paid for the new tram line.
senses.exampleCN: 地方税收收入出资修建了新的有轨电车线路。
senses.why: The same treasury word is narrowed by the adjective local, marking which authority keeps the money.
senses.whyCN: 同一个国库用词被「地方」这个修饰语收窄，标明哪一级当局留下这笔钱。

senses.title: Net revenue after refunds
senses.titleCN: 扣除退税后的净税收收入
senses.definition: the amount left after refunds, credits and arrears are subtracted from gross collections
senses.definitionCN: 从征收总额中扣除退税、抵免与欠缴后剩下的金额
senses.example: Gross receipts looked healthy, but net tax revenue fell after refunds.
senses.exampleCN: 征收总额看着不错，但扣除退税后净税收收入下降了。
senses.why: Accounting separates what is collected from what is kept, so revenue can be reported gross or net.
senses.whyCN: 会计把「收上来」与「留下来」分开，因此收入可分毛额与净额报告。

senses.title: Tax take measured against the economy
senses.titleCN: 以经济总量为基准衡量的税负水平
senses.definition: tax receipts expressed as a proportion of national output, used to compare countries
senses.definitionCN: 以国民产出比例为尺度表示的税收，用于比较各国
senses.example: Tax revenue as a share of output rose three points in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 税收收入占产出的比重在十年间上升了三个百分点。
senses.why: Comparing absolute sums across economies is misleading, so the phrase is turned into a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 直接比较不同经济体的绝对金额会误导，因此这个短语被转换成一个比率。

senses.title: The forecast figure in a budget
senses.titleCN: 预算中的税收收入估算
senses.definition: the projected amount of tax money that a budget expects to receive
senses.definitionCN: 预算预期将收到的税款估算额
senses.example: The forecast for tax revenue was cut by two billion.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中的税收收入估算被下调了二十亿。
senses.why: Governments must plan before money arrives, so revenue also names a number on a projection sheet.
senses.whyCN: 政府必须在钱到手前规划，因此收入也指预测表上的一个数字。

senses.title: Earmarked revenue for a specific purpose
senses.titleCN: 指定用途的专项税收收入
senses.definition: tax money legally reserved for one programme, such as roads or pensions
senses.definitionCN: 依法保留给某一项目使用的税款，如道路或养老金
senses.example: The fuel levy is earmarked tax revenue for road repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料课征是指定用于道路维修的专项税收收入。
senses.why: Once a tax is tied to a purpose, the revenue stops being general and becomes a dedicated stream.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某项税与某个用途绑定，这笔收入就不再是一般财源，而成为专款。

intro.en: Tax revenue joins tax, from Latin taxare 'to assess or charge', with revenue, from Latin revenire 'to come back' through Old French. The pair became standard in public finance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tax revenue 由 tax 与 revenue 合成：tax 出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」，revenue 经古法语来自拉丁 revenire「回来」。这一搭配在公共财政中成为标准说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Taxare 'to assess, charge' gave the noun tax, a levy fixed by authority after a valuation.
items.cn: taxare「评估、课征」给出名词 tax，即经估值后由当局确定的课征。

items.en: Revenire combined re- 'back' with venire 'to come', so the word pictured money coming back to the one who had laid it out.
items.cn: revenire 由「回」加 venire「来」构成，画面是钱回到当初支出它的人手里。

items.en: Old French revenue meant 'a return, an income', and English borrowed it for the income of an estate or a crown.
items.cn: 古法语 revenue 意为「回报、收入」，英语借来表示庄园或王室的收入。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century budgets paired the two words, making tax revenue the standard label for the state's tax income.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的预算把这两个词配在一起，使 tax revenue 成为国家税收收入的标准标签。

items.en: Twentieth-century national accounts turned the phrase into a measured series, reported as a share of output and compared across countries.
items.cn: 二十世纪的国民核算把这个短语变成可测量的序列，按产出比重报告并用于国际比较。

note.en: Group one holds other tax compounds that look alike but measure different things; group two holds words for money coming in.
note.cn: 第一组是形近的其他「税」复合词，但衡量对象不同；第二组是表示进账的词。

entries.definition: The proportion at which income or goods are taxed; it scales the revenue rather than being the revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 指课税的比例，它决定收入的规模，本身不是收入。

entries.definition: The incomes, property or transactions that a tax reaches; revenue is the money actually raised from that base.
entries.definitionCN: 指税所触及的收入、财产或交易；收入是从这个税基实际征得的钱。

entries.definition: The weight of taxation on households or firms; it describes pressure, while revenue describes receipts.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭或企业承受的税负压力；它描述压力，收入描述进账。

entries.definition: The document on which a taxpayer reports income; it is paperwork, not the money collected.
entries.definitionCN: 纳税人申报收入的文件；是文书，不是征得的钱。

entries.definition: Any money received, including fees, fines and sales; tax revenue is the slice that comes from taxes.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指一切收入，包括收费、罚金与销售；税收收入只是来自税的那一部分。

entries.definition: Money received by a person or business; it is not normally used for government receipts.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或企业收到的钱；一般不用来指政府进账。

entries.definition: The money actually received in a period, as recorded by an accountant; close to gross revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 会计记录中某期实际收到的钱，接近毛收入。

entries.definition: The money obtained from a particular sale, event or asset, not from taxation.
entries.definitionCN: 指某笔销售、活动或资产带来的钱，并非来自征税。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Tax plus revenue: what authority charges, and what comes back into the treasury.
normal.cn: 「税」加「回流之物」：当局课征什么，以及什么回到国库。

normal.en: The phrase has a plural for different taxes or years: tax revenues.
normal.cn: 不同税种或年度用复数：各类税收收入。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: total tax revenue, tax revenue growth, a shortfall in tax revenue.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：税收收入总额、税收收入增长、税收收入缺口。

normal.en: Revenue descends from a Latin verb meaning to come back, so the money is pictured returning.
normal.cn: revenue 出自意为「回来」的拉丁动词，因此这笔钱被设想成回流。

normal.en: Statistics compare it as a share of output, not as a raw sum.
normal.cn: 统计上以占产出的比重来比较它，而不是用绝对金额。

abstract.en: Picture a wide river fed by many narrow channels, each named after a different duty.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽河由许多窄渠汇成，每条渠都以一种税命名。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where one bar is drawn longer than all the others combined.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，其中一根长条比其余所有加在一起还长。

abstract.en: Picture a tap that keeps dripping into a public jar while a queue fills cups from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只龙头不断滴进公共的罐子，队伍从罐子里舀水。

examples.en: Rising wages pushed tax revenue above the official forecast.
examples.cn: 工资上涨使税收收入超过了官方预测。

examples.en: The province spends most of its tax revenue on schools and clinics.
examples.cn: 该省把大部分税收收入花在学校与诊所上。

examples.en: A tax revenue shortfall forced the council to delay repairs.
examples.cn: 税收收入缺口迫使议会推迟维修工程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 许多小笔税款汇进国库账本，成为最粗的一栏 → 税收收入

root: 英语复合短语：tax（出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」）+ revenue（经古法语来自拉丁 revenire「回来」，指进账）；指政府征税所得的总金额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow money returning to the treasury: the national total, one tax's yield, central receipts, local receipts, net after refunds, the share of output, the budget forecast, and money tied to a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「钱回流国库」展开：全国总额、单一税种所得、中央收入、地方收入、退税后的净额、占产出的比重、预算估算，以及绑定用途的专款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide river of small payments converging into one treasury ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：由无数小额缴款汇成的一条宽河，最终流进国库账本。

branches.en: COLLECTED MONEY: a total and one tax's share are the same flow at different scales.
branches.cn: 征收所得：总额与单一税种的份额，是同一条水流的不同尺度。

branches.en: LEVEL OF GOVERNMENT: central and local receipts split the same money by who keeps it.
branches.cn: 政府层级：中央与地方收入按「谁留下」把同一笔钱分开。

branches.en: NET FIGURE: refunds carve away part of the inflow before the balance is reported.
branches.cn: 净额：在报告余额之前，退税从流入中挖去一部分。

branches.en: RATIO VIEW: comparing economies turns the sum into a share of output.
branches.cn: 比率视角：比较不同经济体时，金额变成占产出的份额。

branches.en: PLANNED AND TIED: a forecast is money expected, and an earmark is money already promised.
branches.cn: 预算与专款：估算是预期中的钱，专项是已经许诺出去的钱。

intro.en: Tax revenue is an English compound of two Latin-derived words, one for charging and one for money returning.
intro.cn: tax revenue 是由两个源自拉丁语的词构成的英语复合短语，一个指课征，一个指钱回流。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare supplies tax, taxable and taxation; Latin venire supplies revenue, convene and invent through related forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare 给出 tax、taxable 与 taxation；拉丁 venire 经相关形式给出 revenue、convene 与 invent。

items.example: The assessor valued the land for tax.
items.exampleCN: 评估员为征税估定土地价值。

items.example: The root pictures money coming back.

items.example: The city raised the tax on lodging.
Rent is the estate's main revenue.
items.exampleCN: 租金是这份产业的主要收入。
税收收入随工资上涨而增加。

items.example: Only part of the gain is taxable.

items.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构是免税的。

definition_zh: 地表径流；降水在未下渗时沿地表流动形成的水流
definition_en: precipitation that flows over the land surface without infiltrating, before it joins a channel
core_image: 沥青停车场上雨水连成薄片，沿边沟汇聚，几分钟内全部涌入雨水口
scene: 铺了沥青的停车场一落雨就几乎不吸水，水沿边沟汇进排水口。 Paved parking lots shed surface runoff into the storm drains within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 surface runoff 指「未下渗、沿地表面流动的水」（第 1 个义项：与地下流相对、发生在地表界面上的径流）；句意为铺装停车场把地表径流在几分钟内送入雨水口。可辨识物件：沥青面、边沟、雨水篦子、水膜。

pos.zh: 地表径流（不可数，水文用语）

forms.label: 复数（指多次或多种径流事件）

senses.title: The flow on the surface
senses.titleCN: 地表上的流动：与地下流相对
senses.definition: water moving over the ground surface rather than through the soil
senses.definitionCN: 在地表上移动、而非穿过土壤的水
senses.example: Surface runoff begins where rainfall exceeds the soil's capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 地表径流从降雨超过土壤容量的那一刻开始。
senses.why: The two-word term fixes the location: this is the branch of runoff that stays on top, so it can be separated from what sinks.
senses.whyCN: 这个双词术语固定了位置：这是停留在表面的那一支径流，因此可以与下渗部分分开。

senses.title: The storm pulse
senses.definition: the rapid flow produced during intense rain before it reaches a channel
senses.definitionCN: 强降雨期间产生、尚未到达沟道前的快速水流
senses.example: Surface runoff during the downpour exceeded the gutter's capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨期间的地表径流超过了排水沟的容量。
senses.why: Intensity matters more than total depth: short heavy rain outpaces the surface, while gentle rain may never produce this flow at all.
senses.whyCN: 强度比总量更重要：短时强雨超过了地表的吸收速度，而细雨可能根本不产生这种流。

senses.title: The urban version
senses.titleCN: 城市版本：不透水面的产物
senses.definition: rain shed by roofs, roads and paving that must be drained artificially
senses.definitionCN: 由屋顶、道路与铺装排出的雨水，必须靠人工排水
senses.example: Surface runoff from the new district doubled after the fields were paved.
senses.exampleCN: 田地铺上路面后，新城区的地表径流翻了一倍。
senses.why: Paving replaces the soil's entry with a hard plane, so nearly all the rain has to travel sideways.
senses.whyCN: 铺装用硬面取代了土壤的入口，因此几乎所有雨水都只能横向移动。

senses.title: The carrier of farm pollution
senses.definition: the flow that transports soil, fertiliser and pesticide from fields to water bodies
senses.definitionCN: 把泥土、化肥与农药从农田搬到水体的那股水流
senses.example: Surface runoff carries nitrate from the fields into the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 地表径流把农田的硝酸盐带进湖里。
senses.why: This flow is the main non-point route of pollution, because it starts everywhere on a field at once rather than at one pipe.
senses.whyCN: 这股水流是面源污染的主要路径，因为它同时从田地的每一处开始，而不是出自一根管子。

senses.title: The erosion agent
senses.definition: the flow whose energy detaches and carries soil particles downslope
senses.definitionCN: 其能量把土粒剥离并带下坡的水流
senses.example: Surface runoff on the bare slope removed the topsoil in one season.
senses.exampleCN: 裸坡上的地表径流在一个季节内带走了表土。
senses.why: Water only erodes when it moves as a sheet or in rills; once it is spread thin and slow, it carries nothing.
senses.whyCN: 水只有以片流或细沟形式移动时才侵蚀；一旦铺得很薄、流得很慢，它就什么也搬不动。

senses.title: The basin's fast response
senses.definition: the part of a catchment's outflow that arrives quickly after rain
senses.definitionCN: 降雨后迅速到达流域出口的那部分水量
senses.example: Surface runoff set the timing of the flood peak.
senses.exampleCN: 地表径流决定了洪峰出现的时间。
senses.why: Flood forecasting separates the fast surface path from the slow subsurface path, because only the fast one explains a peak within hours.
senses.whyCN: 洪水预报把快的地表路径与慢的地下路径分开，因为只有快路径能解释数小时内出现的洪峰。

senses.title: Rainwater management
senses.definition: the flow that green infrastructure tries to slow, spread or store
senses.definitionCN: 绿色基础设施试图减缓、分散或储存的那股水流
senses.example: Rain gardens are designed to capture surface runoff before it reaches the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水花园的设计目的是在地表径流进入排水口前将其截住。
senses.why: Modern practice treats this flow as a resource to be detained rather than a waste to be piped away.
senses.whyCN: 现代做法把这股水流当作应当滞留的资源，而不是应当用管道排走的废物。

senses.title: Abstract: what stays on the surface
senses.titleCN: 比喻：停留在表面的那部分
senses.definition: a visible, easily moved portion of something that never enters the deeper system
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中可见、易被带走、从未进入更深系统的那部分
senses.example: Most of the debate was surface runoff; the real change happened underground.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争论大多是表层径流，真正的变化发生在地下。
senses.why: The image separates what is visible and fast from what is deep and slow, a distinction that fits many systems.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象把可见而快速的部分与深层而缓慢的部分分开，这种区分适用于许多系统。

intro.en: Surface runoff joins a Latin-derived word for the outer face to a native English verb phrase. The combination is a twentieth-century technical term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: surface runoff 把拉丁来源的「外表面」一词与英语本族动词短语组合起来。这个组合是二十世纪的技术术语。年代为约数。

items.en: Superficies meant the outer face of a body, built from super, above, and facies, form or appearance; French surface and English surface descend from it.
items.cn: superficies 指物体的外表面，由 super「在上方」与 facies「形状、外观」构成；法语 surface 与英语 surface 即由此而来。

items.en: Facies meant shape, face or appearance, not 'to make'; it is a different word from facere, and this is a common source of error.
items.cn: facies 指形状、面容或外观，并非「制造」；它与 facere 是不同的词，此处常被误解。

items.en: The second half is the native verb phrase run off, whose off is an adverb of separation rather than a preposition.
items.cn: 后半部分是本族动词短语 run off，其中的 off 是表示分离的副词，而非介词。

items.en: As catchments came to be modelled separately for surface and subsurface paths, the explicit two-word term became standard.
items.cn: 当流域开始把地表路径与地下路径分开建模时，这个明示的双词术语成为标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation): no standard dictionary fixes the first use of the exact phrase surface runoff, so the dating here is an estimate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：没有通行辞书确定 surface runoff 这一确切短语的首次使用，此处年代只是估计。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that differ by one word; the second holds flow terms that are adjacent in the same system.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个词的短语；第二组是同一系统中相邻的水流术语。

entries.definition: Water that travels laterally below the surface; it is the counterpart, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 在地表以下横向移动的水；是对照项，不是同义词。

entries.definition: Water standing or stored in rivers and lakes; runoff is the moving supply that reaches them.
entries.definitionCN: 停留在河流湖泊中的水；径流是到达它们的流动补给。

entries.definition: The same unchannelled flow, named from the land it crosses rather than the surface it uses.
entries.definitionCN: 同一未成沟的水流，以其穿越的陆地命名，而非以其所在表面命名。

entries.definition: The general term for water flowing off the land, of which the surface path is one branch.
entries.definitionCN: 流离陆地的水的总称，地表路径是其中一支。

entries.definition: Water entering the soil; every drop goes to one path or the other.
entries.definitionCN: 进入土壤的水；每一滴水都走向两者之一。

entries.definition: Rain and its runoff considered as a drainage problem in built areas.
entries.definitionCN: 在建成区被当作排水问题处理的降雨及其径流。

entries.definition: The dry-weather flow fed by groundwater, the opposite timescale to surface runoff.
entries.definitionCN: 由地下水补给的旱季流量，与地表径流的时间尺度相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real words, the Latin facies behind surface, and the pairing with subsurface flow.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实词、surface 背后的拉丁语 facies，以及与地下流的成对关系。

normal.en: surface + runoff says where and what: the flow that stays on the outer face.
normal.cn: surface 加 runoff 同时说明位置与内容：停留在外表面的那股流。

normal.en: surface comes from Latin superficies, super above plus facies face, so it is literally the 'upper face'.
normal.cn: surface 出自拉丁语 superficies，即 super「在上」加 facies「面」，字面就是「上面」。

normal.en: facies means face or appearance, not 'make', so surface has nothing to do with factory.
normal.cn: facies 指面容或外观，不是「制造」，因此 surface 与 factory 无关。

normal.en: The pair is surface runoff and subsurface flow: one over the ground, one through it.
normal.cn: 成对的说法是地表径流与地下流：一个在地面之上，一个穿过地面。

normal.en: Paving turns almost all rain into surface runoff, which is why cities flood faster than fields.
normal.cn: 铺装把几乎所有雨水变成地表径流，所以城市比田野更容易内涝。

abstract.en: Abstractly, this term separates the visible fast layer from the hidden slow one.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，这个术语把可见而快速的表层，与隐藏而缓慢的深层分开。

abstract.en: What stays on the surface is easy to see, easy to measure and easy to blame.
abstract.cn: 停留在表面的东西容易看见、容易测量，也容易被归咎。

abstract.en: Every system has a surface runoff: the part of its activity that never enters its depths.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有它的「表层径流」：那部分从未进入深处的活动。

examples.en: Surface runoff from the construction site silted up the stream for months.
examples.cn: 工地产生的地表径流让这条溪流淤积了数月。

examples.en: The model separates surface runoff from groundwater discharge in the annual budget.
examples.cn: 该模型在年度收支中把地表径流与地下水排泄分开。

examples.en: Wetlands slow surface runoff and let sediment settle before it reaches the lake.
examples.cn: 湿地减缓地表径流，让泥沙在入湖前沉降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「表面（surface）+ 跑掉（run off）」——只在地面表层跑掉的水 → 地表径流

root: 拉丁语 superficies「外表面」（super「在上」+ facies「面」）经法语 surface 进入英语 + 本族动词短语 run off。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one visible flow: the surface branch, its storm pulse, its urban form, its load of farm pollution, its erosion work, its basin response, its place in rainwater design, and finally any visible surplus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一股可见水流展开：地表分支、暴雨脉冲、城市形态、携带的农业污染、侵蚀作用、流域响应、在雨水设计中的位置，最后是任何可见的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a film of rain sliding across asphalt into a gutter and through a drain grate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层雨水滑过沥青面，汇入边沟并穿过雨水篦子。

branches.en: LOCATION AND SPEED: the branch is defined by staying on top, and intensity sets its pace.
branches.cn: 位置与速度：这一支因停留在表面而得名，而强度决定它的快慢。

branches.en: THE PAVED CITY: hard surfaces leave almost no other route.
branches.cn: 铺装的城市：硬质表面几乎不留别的去处。

branches.en: CARRIER AND CUTTER: the flow moves fertiliser and also removes soil.
branches.cn: 搬运与切割：这股流既搬走肥料，也削去土壤。

branches.en: FAST RESPONSE AND DESIGN: it sets flood timing, and green infrastructure tries to detain it.
branches.cn: 快速响应与设计：它决定洪水时序，而绿色基础设施试图滞留它。

branches.en: VISIBLE SURPLUS: what never enters the depths stays on the face and moves quickly.
branches.cn: 可见的剩余：从未进入深处的东西留在表面，移动得很快。

intro.en: The phrase mixes a Latin-derived noun with a native verb phrase, so it shows both layers of English vocabulary in one term.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的名词与本族动词短语混在一起，因此在一个术语里同时显示英语词汇的两个层次。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is superficies, from super above and facies face; facies is not related to facere, to make. The second element has no Latin root at all.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 superficies，由 super「在上」与 facies「面」构成；facies 与 facere「制造」并无关联。第二个成分完全没有拉丁词根。

definition_zh: v. 遵守；服从
definition_en: to act in accordance with a rule or request
core_image: 工厂门口的告示牌旁，工人戴上安全帽
scene: 新规定生效后，工厂必须按时遵守。 When the new rules took effect, the factory had to comply.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：comply 指遵守；句意是新规定生效后，工厂必须按时遵守。

senses.title: To follow a rule
senses.definition: to do what a rule, law or order requires
senses.definitionCN: 按规则、法律或命令去做
senses.example: All staff must comply with the safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工必须遵守安全规范。
senses.why: Latin complere means to fill up or fulfil.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为填满、履行。

senses.definitionCN: 顺从某人的要求

senses.exampleCN: 他一言不发地照做了。
senses.why: The sense shifts from fulfilling rules to yielding.
senses.whyCN: 该义从履行规则转向顺从他人。

intro.en: Comply comes from a Latin verb meaning to fulfil or fill up.
intro.cn: comply 源自拉丁语「履行、填满」的动词。

items.cn: complere 意为填满、履行。

items.cn: 法语 complir 意为履行。

abstract.en: A form filled in completely.

abstract.en: A rule met without argument.

sensesIntro.en: To fulfil a rule, and to yield to a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 履行规则，以及顺从他人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worker putting on a helmet beside a notice board
core.cn: 核心意象：工人在告示牌旁戴上安全帽

branches.en: A helmet worn as required.
branches.cn: 按要求戴上的安全帽。

branches.en: A form filled out on time.
branches.cn: 按时填好的表格。

branches.en: A request met without words.
branches.cn: 一言不发地照办。

branches.cn: 一个点头与一个签名。

branches.en: Meeting what is asked, rule or person.

definition_zh: 建筑风格；某一时期或地域的建筑形制与审美特征；建筑史中的风格分类
definition_en: the characteristic forms, proportions and ornaments shared by buildings of a period, place or movement
core_image: 同一条街上并列着尖拱、圆拱与方盒子，一眼就能看出它们属于不同年代
scene: 街上并排着尖顶石屋、圆顶教堂和一排玻璃方楼。 A guide uses each facade to explain a different architectural style without naming a single date.
sceneCN: 这里 architectural style 指「某一时期或流派在建筑上共有的形制与审美特征」（第 1 个义项：建筑风格的总称）；句意为导游借每一面立面讲一种不同的建筑风格，却一个年代都不提。图中可辨识物件：尖顶石屋、圆顶教堂、玻璃方楼、街面。

pos.zh: 建筑风格（可数名词短语）

senses.title: The shared look of a period
senses.definition: the set of forms, proportions and ornaments that buildings of one period share
senses.definitionCN: 同一时期的建筑在形制、比例与装饰上共有的那一套特征
senses.example: The whole quarter keeps one architectural style, down to the window frames.
senses.exampleCN: 整个街区保持同一种建筑风格，连窗框也不例外。
senses.why: style here means a recognizable family resemblance, so the phrase names what makes a group of buildings look related.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 style 指可辨认的家族相似，因此短语命名的是让一群建筑看起来同源的东西。

senses.title: The classical orders
senses.definition: the system of Doric, Ionic and Corinthian columns with fixed proportions and entablatures
senses.definitionCN: 由多立克、爱奥尼与科林斯柱式连同固定比例与檐部构成的体系
senses.example: The bank chose an architectural style of columns and pediments to look permanent.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行选用带柱与山花的古典建筑风格，好显得恒久。
senses.why: classical style is a grammar with rules, so a building can be correct or incorrect within it.
senses.whyCN: 古典风格是一套有规则的语法，因此一栋建筑在其中可以被判为合规或不合规。

senses.title: Romanesque and Gothic
senses.definition: the medieval styles marked first by heavy round arches and then by pointed arches and ribbed vaults
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪风格，先以厚重的圆拱为标志，后以尖拱与肋拱顶为标志
senses.example: The nave shows how an architectural style can change within one building campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这座中殿显示，一种建筑风格在同一次建造中也会发生变化。
senses.why: the structural problem of height and light drove both styles, so their differences are engineering as much as taste.
senses.whyCN: 高度与采光的结构难题推动了这两种风格，因此它们的差别既是工程也是审美。

senses.title: Renaissance and Baroque
senses.definition: the styles that revived classical order and then stretched it into movement, curve and display
senses.definitionCN: 先复兴古典秩序、再把它拉向动感、曲线与铺陈的风格
senses.example: The palace mixes an architectural style of calm symmetry with a Baroque staircase.
senses.exampleCN: 这座宫殿把平静对称的建筑风格与一道巴洛克楼梯混在一起。
senses.why: each style answers the one before it, so the phrase also names a position in an argument about proportion.
senses.whyCN: 每种风格都在回应前一种，因此这个短语也标记了一场关于比例的论辩中的立场。

senses.title: Modernism and the international style
senses.definition: the twentieth-century style of plain surfaces, exposed structure and refusal of ornament
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪那种表面素净、结构外露并拒绝装饰的风格
senses.example: Critics said the new library had no architectural style at all, only a grid.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家说新图书馆根本没有建筑风格，只有一张网格。
senses.why: modernism claimed to end style, yet its rules became a style recognizable enough to be named and copied.
senses.whyCN: 现代主义声称终结风格，但它的规则本身成了足够可辨、可被命名与模仿的一种风格。

senses.title: Regional and vernacular building
senses.definition: the local forms that grow from climate, material and craft rather than from a named movement
senses.definitionCN: 由气候、材料与手艺生长出来、而非出自某个有名流派的地方形制
senses.example: The island has an architectural style of low walls and thick whitewash.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛有一种低墙厚白灰的建筑风格。
senses.why: vernacular style is learned by copying neighbours, so it is a style without an author.
senses.whyCN: 乡土风格靠模仿邻里习得，因此是一种没有作者的风格。

senses.title: A dating tool in art history
senses.definition: a category scholars use to place a building in time, region or school
senses.definitionCN: 学者用来把建筑放入某个年代、地区或流派的分类范畴
senses.example: A single carved capital can fix the architectural style of a ruined church.
senses.exampleCN: 一个雕花柱头就能定下一座废教堂的建筑风格。
senses.why: once style is used for dating, the phrase stops describing a look and starts making a claim about history.
senses.whyCN: 一旦风格被用于断代，这个短语就不再描述外观，而在对历史作出判断。

senses.title: The frame of any work
senses.titleCN: 泛指作品的整体构造方式
senses.definition: the overall organizing manner of a work, argument or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作品、论证或组织整体的组织方式
senses.example: The report has an architectural style of its own: broad base, narrow top, no ornament.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告有自己的一套构造风格：底盘宽、顶部窄、不加装饰。
senses.why: the metaphor works because any built thing, physical or not, must decide what carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，因为任何被建造之物，不论是否实体，都必须决定由什么承重。

intro.en: The phrase joins the Latin-derived word for building art to a Latin word for a writing tool whose meaning drifted into 'manner'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自拉丁语的「建筑之术」与一个拉丁语「书写工具」词连起来，后者的意义漂移为「方式」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Architectura named the art of the architect, built on the Greek compound for chief builder.
items.cn: architectura 指建筑师之术，其基础是表示「匠师首领」的希腊语复合词。

items.en: Stilus was the pointed metal tool used to write on wax tablets; by transfer it came to mean the manner of writing.
items.cn: stilus 是蜡板上书写用的尖金属笔；经转喻，它开始指书写的方式。

items.en: The English spelling style reflects the influence of Greek stulos 'column', which is a spelling loan and not the source of the word.
items.cn: 英语拼写 style 受希腊语 stulos「柱子」影响，但这只是拼写上的借形，并非词源。

items.en: Writers on art began to speak of the style of a building, meaning the manner its parts were handled.
items.cn: 十六世纪的艺术写作者开始谈某座建筑的 style，指其各部分被处理的方式。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the phrase became a technical label for periods and schools, such as Gothic or Romanesque.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个短语成为指称时期与流派的技术标签，如哥特式或罗曼式。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of stilus before Latin is not established, and the link sometimes proposed to a verb for 'pricking' remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：stilus 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，有人提出它与表示「刺」的动词有关，那仍只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds terms that look like style words but name different things; group two holds words for the same idea seen from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来像风格词、实则指别的东西的术语；第二组是从另一角度看同一概念的说法。

entries.definition: The pointed writing tool that gave style its name; it is a physical object, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 给 style 命名的尖头书写工具，是实物，而非方式。

entries.definition: Relating to style as a quality; a stylistic choice is a choice about manner, not a named period.
entries.definitionCN: 指与风格这一属性相关的；风格上的选择是关于方式的选择，而非某个有名时期。

entries.definition: Simplified according to an artistic convention; it describes a treatment, not a building tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种艺术惯例加以简化；描述处理手法，而非建筑传统。

entries.definition: The discipline or the built result; two buildings of the same architecture can differ in style.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或建成成果；同属一种建筑学传统的两栋建筑，风格仍可不同。

entries.definition: The fixed proportions of columns and entablature; an order is one possible basis of a style, not the style itself.
entries.definitionCN: 柱与檐部的固定比例；柱式只是某种风格可能的基础，而非风格本身。

entries.definition: A way of building passed between generations; it stresses method and training more than visual identity.
entries.definitionCN: 代代相传的建造方式；更强调方法与训练，而非视觉特征。

entries.definition: A contemporary term for a consistent set of forms across products or buildings; it avoids the period claims of style.
entries.definitionCN: 当代术语，指产品与建筑中共用的一套形制；它回避了 style 所带的时代断言。

entries.definition: The everyday word for visible appearance; it carries no claim about period, rules or school.
entries.definitionCN: 指可见外观的日常词，不含年代、规则或流派方面的断言。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin sources, the real period labels and the real art-history use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语来源、真实的时期标签与真实的艺术史用法。

normal.en: Architecture gives the field; style gives the manner; together they name the manner of a building family.
normal.cn: architecture 给领域，style 给方式，合起来指一个建筑家族的做事方式。

normal.en: The family runs style, stylistic, stylize, stylized, stylus.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 style、stylistic、stylize、stylized、stylus。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the periods: Gothic, classical, modern, regional architectural style.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把时期分开：哥特式、古典式、现代式、地域性建筑风格。

normal.en: The pointed writing tool and the Greek word for column both shaped the spelling of style.
normal.cn: 尖头书写工具与希腊语「柱子」一词都影响了 style 的拼写。

normal.en: Art historians date a building by its smallest carved detail, not by its size.
normal.cn: 艺术史家靠最小的雕饰细节而非体量来给建筑断代。

abstract.en: Picture three generations standing in one doorway, each wearing the coat of their own decade.
abstract.cn: 想象三代人站在同一道门里，各自穿着自己那个年代的外套。

abstract.en: Picture a language whose grammar is made of stone, so every sentence must be built before it is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一种语法由石头构成的语言，每句话都得先建起来才能说出。

abstract.en: Picture a family album where every house is a self-portrait of the person who paid for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭相册，每栋房子都是出钱建造者的自画像。

examples.en: The station borrows its architectural style from the town hall across the square.
examples.cn: 这座车站的建筑风格借自广场对面的市政厅。

examples.en: No single architectural style dominates the old port, which grew in waves.
examples.cn: 老港区没有哪一种建筑风格占主导，它是分几波扩建起来的。

examples.en: Students must identify the architectural style from a photograph of one window.
examples.cn: 学生要凭一张窗户照片判断建筑风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: architectural（建筑的）+ style（风格）→ 建筑上的那套做法与样子 → 建筑风格

root: architectural 源自拉丁 architectura「建筑之术」；style 源自拉丁 stilus「蜡板刻写笔」，转指书写方式；拼写受希腊 stulos「柱子」影响。英语 architectural style。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: what makes a group of buildings look related? The answer moves from a shared look, through named periods and rules, to a dating tool and finally to any constructed frame.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个问题展开：是什么让一群建筑看起来同源？答案从共同外观，经有名时期与规则，走到断代工具，最后落到任何被构造的框架上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one street holds three centuries at once, and each facade tells you its own date without a plaque.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上同时站着三个世纪，每面立面都不用铭牌就说出自己的年代。

branches.en: RESEMBLANCE: the phrase begins with the plain fact that certain buildings look like relatives.
branches.cn: 相似：这个短语从「某些建筑看起来像亲戚」这一朴素事实开始。

branches.en: RULES AND STRUCTURE: columns follow a grammar, while arches answer a problem of height and light.
branches.cn: 规则与结构：柱式遵循一套语法，而拱券回应高度与采光的难题。

branches.en: REVIVAL AND REFUSAL: one style revives the past, the next claims to have no style at all.
branches.cn: 复兴与拒绝：一种风格复兴过去，下一种则声称自己根本没有风格。

branches.en: HABIT WITHOUT AN AUTHOR: local building and any constructed frame show style as an organizing manner.
branches.cn: 没有作者的习惯：乡土建造与任何被构造的框架，都把风格显示为一种组织方式。

branches.en: THE LABEL: scholars turn the look into a tool for placing a building in time.
branches.cn: 标签：学者把外观变成一种把建筑放回时间里的工具。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin noun of building with a Latin noun of writing that became a noun of manner, so each half has its own derivational family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个拉丁语「建筑」名词与一个由「书写」转为「方式」的拉丁语名词组合起来，两半各有自己的派生家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin architectura and stilus both passed into English through French, and stilus also gave the doublet stylus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 architectura 与 stilus 都经法语进入英语，而 stilus 还给出了同源异形词 stylus。

items.example: Architectura covered design and construction alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时涵盖设计与施工。

items.example: The drawing is an architectural record.
items.exampleCN: 这张图是一份建筑记录。

items.example: The architecture of the station is austere.
items.exampleCN: 这座车站的建筑风格很朴素。

items.meaning: a pointed writing tool; manner of writing
items.meaningCN: 尖头书写工具；书写方式
items.example: Stilus meant the tool before it meant the manner.
items.exampleCN: stilus 先指工具，后指方式。

items.example: The style of the porch is unmistakable.
items.exampleCN: 这道门廊的风格不会认错。

items.example: The change is stylistic rather than structural.
items.exampleCN: 这一改动属于风格层面，而非结构层面。

items.meaning: to treat in a simplified artistic manner
items.meaningCN: 按简化的艺术方式处理
items.example: The sculptor stylized the leaves into flat fans.
items.exampleCN: 雕刻家把叶子处理成扁平的扇面。

items.meaning: a pointed instrument for writing or touching
items.meaningCN: 书写或触控用的尖头工具
items.example: A stylus scratched the wax tablet.

latinEntries.meaning: pointed writing tool; manner of writing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 尖头书写工具；书写方式

definition_zh: 有抱负的；渴望的；求职者；候选人
definition_en: aiming for a high position or goal, or a person who seeks such a position
core_image: 盯着录取名单、眼里有光的年轻人
scene: 考场上，每个屏息落笔的人都盼着金榜题名。 Each aspirant waited outside the office for the final interview.
sceneCN: 这里 aspirant 是名词「候选人、有志者」（第 2 个义项：谋求高位的人）；句意是每位候选人在办公室外等待最终面试。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词（拉丁语 aspirare），义为「渴望；追求」
同根名词，义为「志向；渴望」
由 aspiration 派生，义为「有雄心壮志的」

senses.title: Full of ambition
senses.definition: ambitious and striving toward a goal or high position
senses.definitionCN: 怀有雄心、朝目标或高位努力
senses.example: The studio is full of aspirant directors shooting short films.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室里挤满了拍摄短片的、雄心勃勃的准导演。
senses.why: Latin aspirare meant to breathe toward; ambition was imagined as breath reaching toward a goal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aspirare 意为朝…呼气；雄心被想象为向目标呼出的气息。

senses.title: A person seeking advancement
senses.definition: one who seeks a position, honor, or office
senses.definitionCN: 谋求职位、荣誉或官职的人
senses.example: Party aspirants competed for the nomination.
senses.exampleCN: 党内竞争者角逐提名。
senses.why: When the striving is personified, the adjective becomes the noun for the striver.
senses.whyCN: 当这种奋斗被拟人化，形容词就名词化为「奋斗者」。

intro.en: Aspirant comes from Latin aspirare, to breathe toward, formed of ad- plus spirare, to breathe.
intro.cn: aspirant 源自拉丁语 aspirare（向…呼气），由 ad-（朝向）加 spirare（呼吸）构成。

items.en: The root *speis- meant to blow or breathe.
items.cn: 词根 *speis- 意为吹、呼吸。

items.en: Spirare meant to breathe, giving spirit, inspire, respire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸，派生 spirit、inspire、respire。

items.en: Aspirare meant to breathe on or toward, later to seek eagerly.
items.cn: aspirare 意为向…吹气，后引申为热切追求。

items.en: Aspirer kept the figurative pursuit sense.
items.cn: 古法语 aspirer 保留追求的比喻义。

items.en: English formed the noun aspirant for a seeker of high office.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪英语由之构成名词 aspirant，指谋求高位者。

note.en: Aspirant names the person behind the verb aspire: the one still climbing.
note.cn: aspirant 是动词 aspire 背后的人：那个仍在攀登的人。

entries.definition: a strong desire for achievement
entries.definitionCN: 志向；渴望

entries.definition: showing or aiming at ambition
entries.definitionCN: 励志的；令人向往的

entries.definition: to breathe out, hence to end
entries.definitionCN: 到期；断气（同根反衬）

entries.definition: the act of breathing
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸

entries.definition: similar ending, different Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩（后缀相似，词根不同）

entries.definition: one who seeks an office or position
entries.definitionCN: 候选人

entries.definition: one who competes for something
entries.definitionCN: 竞争者

entries.definition: one who tries to find or obtain
entries.definitionCN: 寻求者

entries.definition: one making a claim, as to a title
entries.definitionCN: 要求者；索赔人

entries.definition: a person likely to succeed, informal
entries.definitionCN: 有望成功者（口语）

normalIntro.en: See aspire inside: an aspirant is one who aspires, still out of breath from climbing.
normalIntro.cn: aspir（aspire 渴望）+ ant（者）：仍在攀爬、喘着气追梦的人。

normal.en: spirare is breath: spirit, inspire, respire.
normal.cn: spirare 是呼吸：spirit、inspire、respire。

normal.en: ad- + spirare: breathe toward a goal.
normal.cn: ad- + spirare：向目标呼气，即追求。

normal.en: -ant turns the verb into the person.
normal.cn: -ant 把动词变成人。

normal.en: expire breathes out, ends; aspire breathes toward.
normal.cn: expire 呼出即终结；aspire 朝向即追求。

normal.en: an aspirant has not yet arrived.
normal.cn: aspirant 尚未抵达终点。

abstract.en: Picture lungs filling before a sprint.
abstract.cn: 想象冲刺前深深吸气的肺。

abstract.en: See names on a shortlist, one circled in red.
abstract.cn: 看见入围名单上一个被红笔圈起的名字。

abstract.en: Feel the upward pull of a summit above clouds.
abstract.cn: 感受云巅向上的牵引。

examples.en: Every aspirant dreamed of playing at the nationals.
examples.cn: 每位有志者都梦想参加全国大赛。

examples.en: The think tank hired several aspirant economists.
examples.cn: 智库聘用了几位雄心勃勃的青年经济学者。

examples.en: Aspirants for the scholarship submitted essays in March.
examples.cn: 奖学金申请者三月份提交了论文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿斯派任特」——饿着也派自己去任重职，正是 aspirant 的进取心。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ spirare（呼吸）→ aspirare「向目标呼气、热望」，后缀 -ant 表人。

sensesIntro.en: Breathing toward becomes striving for, and the striver becomes a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 「向之呼气」化为「为之奋斗」，奋斗者进而名词化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath drawn toward a summit still out of reach
core.cn: 核心意象：朝尚未企及的山峰呼出的气息

branches.en: the ambitious quality
branches.cn: 有抱负的特质

branches.en: the person seeking the goal
branches.cn: 追求目标的人

branches.en: climbing that is not yet done
branches.cn: 尚未完成的攀登

branches.en: competition for office or honor
branches.cn: 对职位或荣誉的竞争

branches.en: the drive behind early careers
branches.cn: 早期职业生涯背后的动力

intro.en: The spirare family spreads through English words of breath, life, and ambition.
intro.cn: spirare 词族遍布英语中关于呼吸、生命与抱负的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare anchors one of English's most productive roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 是英语最高产的词根之一。

items.meaning: to breathe through, hence to happen

definition_zh: adj. 恰当的，贴切的；易于……的，有……倾向的；（学生）聪慧的，一学就会的
definition_en: Exactly suited to the purpose or occasion; inclined or liable to do something; of a learner, quick to pick things up.
core_image: 正好合得上那个槽口，一放就到位
scene: 这个比喻用得恰到好处。 It was an apt metaphor for a fragile economy.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apt 指某句话或某个说法正好贴合眼下的情形，不多不少。

senses.title: Exactly suited
senses.definition: so well fitted to the situation that it seems made for it, used of words, names and comparisons
senses.definitionCN: 与情形贴合得仿佛专为它而造，用于词语、名称与比喻
senses.example: Silence was the aptest reply he could give.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默是他能给出的最贴切的回答。
senses.why: The Latin source means fastened or fitted, so an apt phrase is one that clicks into the situation like a part into its slot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「装好的、合上的」，所以 apt 的说法就像零件卡进槽口一样合上眼下的情形。

senses.title: Inclined or liable
senses.definition: having a tendency to do something, in the pattern apt to plus a verb
senses.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，用于 apt to 加动词的句式
senses.example: Old pipes are apt to burst in a hard frost.
senses.exampleCN: 旧水管在严寒中容易爆裂。
senses.why: If a thing fits a slot, it slides there easily, so fitted turns into likely: the behaviour is the groove it naturally runs in.
senses.whyCN: 东西合得上槽口就容易滑进去，于是「合上」引申为「易于」：那种行为就是它天然会走的沟槽。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: of a person, especially a pupil, ready and able to take in new skills
senses.definitionCN: 指人尤其是学生，能迅速接受新技能
senses.example: She was an apt student of the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她学小提琴一点就通。
senses.why: Here the fit is between the learner and the subject: the mind takes the shape of what it is taught without resistance.
senses.whyCN: 这里合得上的是学习者与所学：头脑毫无阻力地长成所教内容的形状。

intro.en: Apt is Latin aptus, fitted, the past participle of apere, to fasten. The same root gives adapt, adept, inept and aptitude.
intro.cn: apt 就是拉丁语 aptus「合好的」，是 apere「系紧、装上」的过去分词。同一词根产生 adapt、adept、inept 与 aptitude。

items.en: Latin apere meant to fasten or attach one thing to another, a verb of joining rather than of choosing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 apere 意为「把一物系到另一物上」，是表「连接」而非「挑选」的动词。

items.en: The participle aptus meant fastened, hence fitted and suitable: the part is already in its place.
items.cn: 过去分词 aptus 意为「系好的」，进而指「合适的」：零件已经就位。

items.en: Greek haptein, to fasten, is a cousin of apere, which shows the root is older than Latin itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 haptein「系紧」与 apere 同源，说明这个词根比拉丁语本身更古老。

items.en: English borrowed apt in the late fourteenth century for something suited to its purpose.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末借入 apt，表示某物与其用途相合。

items.en: Around the 1590s apt gained the sense of prone or liable, and also the sense of a quick learner.
items.cn: 1590 年代前后，apt 增加了「易于、往往」之义，也增加了「学得快」之义。

items.en: The same root builds adapt, to fit to, adept, thoroughly fitted, and inept, not fitted at all.
items.cn: 同一词根构成 adapt「使合上」、adept「完全合上、熟练」与 inept「完全合不上、笨拙」。

note.en: The look-alike group is a family lesson: adept is skilled, inept is clumsy, adapt is to make fit; the near-meaning group gives the plain synonyms.
note.cn: 形近组是一堂家族课：adept 是熟练，inept 是笨拙，adapt 是使合适；近义组给出朴素同义词。

normalIntro.en: Apt means fitted: a phrase that fits the moment, a habit that fits the person, a mind that fits the subject.
normalIntro.cn: apt 的本意是「合得上」：说法合得上此刻，习惯合得上这人，头脑合得上这门学问。

normal.en: Apt to plus a verb means likely to.
normal.cn: apt to 加动词意为「易于、往往」。

normal.en: Comparative and superlative are apter and aptest.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 apter、aptest。

normal.en: The adverb is aptly, as in aptly named.
normal.cn: 副词是 aptly，如 aptly named「名副其实」。

normal.en: Adept is skilled; inept is clumsy; do not mix them.
normal.cn: adept 是熟练，inept 是笨拙，别混。

normal.en: Apt is short and formal; suitable is the safe everyday word.
normal.cn: apt 简短而正式，suitable 是稳妥的日常词。

abstract.cn: 想象钥匙滑进属于它的那把锁。

abstract.en: Imagine a nickname that fits like a glove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴得像手套的外号。

abstract.en: Think of a groove a ball keeps rolling back into.

examples.cn: 书名很贴切：这本书写的确实就是等待。

examples.en: He is apt to promise more than he can deliver.

sensesIntro.en: The three senses are one fit: words fitting a moment, a person fitting a habit, and a mind fitting a subject.

branches.en: A nickname that fits perfectly.
